name: Crucible Industries Storm-12 'Thunderclap'
description:
The Crucible Industries Storm-12 is a semi-automatic shotgun chambered in 12 gauge with a gas-operated action and a seven-round detachable box magazine. The weapon features a full-length Picatinny rail, adjustable stock, and a heavy-profile barrel with an integral breaching muzzle device. Every surface communicates tactical intent — this is not a hunting shotgun repurposed for combat, but a purpose-built combat shotgun from the ground up.

The Thunderclap's gas system is tuned to cycle reliably with everything from light birdshot to heavy magnum slugs without adjustment — a significant engineering achievement that most shotguns require manual gas port adjustment to match. The detachable box magazine allows rapid reloading compared to tube-fed designs, and spare magazines can be carried on standard plate-carrier pouches. The system transforms the shotgun from a slow-reloading specialty weapon into a primary combat arm with practical sustained fire capability.

Crucible Industries markets the Storm-12 to corponation tactical teams and licensed security contractors who need breaching and close-quarters capability. The integral breaching device allows the weapon to be placed against a door hinge and fired to remove the hinge — a specialized function that the Thunderclap performs while remaining a fully functional combat shotgun. This dual-purpose design has made it standard equipment for breach teams throughout GLMZ.
specifications:
caliber: 12 gauge
effective_range: 40 meters (slug), 25 meters (buckshot)
rate_of_fire: Semi-automatic
magazine_capacity: 7 rounds (detachable box)
weight: 3.6 kg
tactical_use: A combat shotgun designed for breaching and close-quarters operations. The semi-automatic action provides rapid follow-up shots. The detachable magazine enables fast reloading. The integral breaching device allows door-hinge removal without switching weapons. The universal gas system handles all ammunition types without adjustment. Effective as a primary weapon for CQB operations.
cultural_context: The Thunderclap is the weapon that comes through your door. In GLMZ's collective consciousness, the sound of a Storm-12 breaching a hinge is associated with corponation enforcement actions — raids, repossessions, and 'security interventions' that nobody in the target neighborhood requested. The weapon's reputation is functional, efficient, and deeply unwelcome.
story_hooks: A Thunderclap is used to breach a door that turns out to be booby-trapped — the breaching charge detonates a secondary device that kills the breach team. Someone knew exactly which weapon would be used and how.
Crucible Industries recalls a batch of Storm-12s after discovering the gas system has a flaw that causes the weapon to slam-fire — emptying the magazine uncontrollably after the first shot.

physical_description.visual_profile: A brutalist combat shotgun with aggressive angular geometry. The Storm-12 presents a compact, purpose-built silhouette dominated by its heavy barrel and integral breaching muzzle. The full-length Picatinny rail runs the length of the top, creating a clean datum line that emphasizes the weapon's modular, tactical character. The adjustable stock extends the rear profile, and the detachable box magazine protrudes prominently beneath the action — a visible statement of reload-speed engineering.
physical_description.dimensions: Total length: 92 cm (stock collapsed) to 105 cm (fully extended). Barrel length: 51 cm with integral breaching device. Magazine well: 8 cm deep. Height over rail: 7 cm.
physical_description.weight_description: Hefty but well-balanced. The 3.6 kg mass is distributed forward into the heavy-profile barrel and breaching device, creating natural point-of-aim stability. Not light, but the ergonomic design prevents it from feeling unwieldy in tactical use.
physical_description.primary_material: Aircraft-grade 7075-T6 aluminum alloy receiver with steel barrel and breaching muzzle assembly. Polymer furniture (foregrip, cheek rest) is reinforced nylon composite rated for impact.
physical_description.finish: Matte anodized black aluminum with a textured, non-reflective surface. The steel barrel exhibits a dull parkerized gray-black finish. Breaching muzzle shows wear-resistant hard-coat anodizing in flat charcoal.
physical_description.color_scheme: Flat tactical black with charcoal-gray accents on the muzzle device and rail surfaces. Some units show ghost-ring sights in matte stainless or tritium-filled wells.
physical_description.grip_texture: Textured polymer pistol grip with aggressive vertical ribbing for positive purchase even in wet conditions. The foregrip features deep checkering. Gas tube beneath the barrel has a smooth machined finish.
distinctive_features: Integral dual-port breaching muzzle device with reinforced steel face for hinge-removal strikes
Full-length Picatinny rail with integrated iron sight mounts (ghost ring rear, ramp front)
Prominent detachable box magazine with numbered witness holes for round-count visibility
Gas-port regulator dial beneath the barrel (unmarked, set at factory)
Charging handle positioned on left side of receiver, oversized for gloved operation
Bolt-release lever integrated into trigger guard
Heat vent slots along foregrip to manage barrel heat
Sling attachment points at receiver and stock
Serial number plate mounted on left side of receiver below rail
Corpus-red Crucible Industries logo stamp on grip and receiver
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Crucible Industries stylized Φ logo (QUANTA symbol doubled as brand mark) stamped in red anodize on left grip panel. 'STORM-12 THUNDERCLAP' engraved in block letters on barrel above gas tube. Serial number on machined stainless steel plate riveted to lower receiver. 'CRUCIBLE INDUSTRIES / GLMZ' micro-etched on breaching muzzle face.
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained field condition. Scratch patterns on Picatinny rail from optic/accessory mounting and dismounting. Breaching muzzle shows scuffing and minor deformation from contact with door frames. Magazine witness holes exhibit carbon-buildup staining. Rail surfaces retain matte finish; receiver may show minor operational wear. Chrome plating on internal components visible through ejection port.
